title: Cuneiform Tablet
intro: This is a clay tablet covered in cuneiform, one of the world's earliest writing systems. Scribes pressed a reed into wet clay to make each wedge-shaped mark.
provenance: Exact findspot not recorded in this catalogue entry.
facts: Cuneiform means wedge-shaped, after the marks a reed stylus leaves in clay.
The script began as pictures used to keep accounts and later wrote many languages.
Clay tablets survive fire far better than paper, so many have lasted thousands of years.
Most tablets record everyday things such as trade, debts and rations, not only royal events.
unknown: The text on this particular tablet is not translated in this catalogue entry, and its author is not recorded.
